reason: The hypothesis restates the well-known dynamic deformation mechanism of FCC high-entropy alloys—a transition from thermally activated glide to phonon drag and twinning with increasing strain rate—that is already reported as a result in multiple passages (P2, P3, P7, P8, P17, P24, P26, P28, P31, P40) for similar alloys. Applying it to the Co-free FeNiCrMn system is a minor compositional change without new mechanistic justification, making the core idea a restatement of existing findings.
copied_elements: shift in deformation mechanism with strain rate/temperature
thermally activated dislocation glide at low strain rates
phonon drag at high strain rates
deformation twinning at high strain rates
increase in yield strength and strain hardening with strain rate
microstructural evidence of transition (dislocation density, twins)
